change_summary: PLOS ONE retracted this paper, the notice's title being 'Retraction: Detecting phishing websites using machine learning technique'. The editors retracted it because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process, and the notice says these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. The author either did not respond or could not be reached. The whole article is retracted and its results are in question, so its findings cannot be relied on.
evaluation: Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, relying on the reported LURL accuracy, and PLOS ONE has retracted that whole article, saying the validity and provenance of its reported results are in question. Your Section 4 also starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14], and these come from the same retracted paper, so this use is touched too. Overall the impact on your draft is high, because both your design rationale and your starting settings rest on the retracted paper.
recommendation: Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, and your Section 4 starts from its settings, while PLOS ONE retracted the whole article and says the validity and provenance of its reported results are in question. Raise the Section 4 dependency with your co-authors or supervisor before building further on those settings. Remove or replace the Section 3 citation and re-check the LSTM choice, and cite the retraction notice if the paper stays in the reference list.
